newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks open lower in mixed trade.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks open lower in mixed trade.

text.p: * Toronto stocks opened lower in mixed trade on Friday, with rising consumer products and golds offset by losses in nearly all other sectors. * 6.6 million shares traded.
Toronto stocks opened lower as expected on Friday as rising consumer products and golds were offset by losses in nearly every other sector.

Traders said overall volumes were thin as market players all watched the same few issues, amid rumored takeover talks between Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce and Canada Trust, whose parent company, CT Financial Services Inc, is a unit of Imasco Ltd.
"There's not a lot of yelling and screaming this morning, volumes are very small...I think everybody is watching the same five stocks on their screens this morning," one said.
CT Financial was halted on the Toronto Stock Exchange, while Imasco rose 2.85 to 44.50 in early trade before settling to 43.10. Shares in CIBC were down 0.35 at 37.30 in active trade.
The trader said the banks were the most watched group on Friday as the sector continued to flex its merger muscles.

Sources told Reuters CIBC is set to announce next week that it will acquire mid-sized U.S. brokerage Oppenheimer & Co. for about US$500 million, close on the heels of a major move by Royal Bank into the Canadian insurance industry.
The TSE 300 Composite Index fell 15.2 points to 6739.93 at the open in turnover of 6.6 million shares worth C$123.9 million. Advances outpaced declines 220 to 202, while 214 issues traded unchanged.
Eleven of Toronto's 14 sub-indexes lost ground, led by banks, industrials and transportation, which all lost more than one percent in early trade.
Consumer products, golds and pipelines rose.
